document.title: Source Card Deck — 20 MPC + 10 Leverage Dynamics v0.1

paragraphs.text: Week 1 • 20 MPC canon anchors + 10 Leverage/social-influence case dynamics • v0.1

These cards turn the source library into scene-ready material. MPC cards define the project’s positive theology and practice; case-dynamic cards supply institutional pressure, uncanny social perception, and epistemic conflict.
Retrieve 2–4 MPC cards and 1–2 case-dynamic cards for a scene.
Write the scene’s observable event before choosing its explanation.
Make the teaching causal: a practice changes what a character can perceive, choose, or repair.
Record every fictional transformation in the transformation log.
A. MPC theological and practice cards
MPC-01 — Chastity integrates desire toward love
Chastity gathers the sexual drive and passions into whole-person love; it makes the other visible as a person rather than an object.
An almost-kiss becomes more intimate when Mara stops scanning for status and actually sees Jonah’s fatigue, restraint, and delight.
Satisfied in God, VA Beach, Nov 2025 — Session 4 • mpc-74e7842c6f30540d8f5a-b000036 • [open source](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1063365119)
MPC-02 — The riverbanks, not the dam
Chastity is not suppression or mere restraint; it gives desire direction, like banks giving form to a stream.
A mentor rejects Mara’s attempt to become numb and instead asks what her desire is trying to move toward.
Ordered desire reduces inner tension and creates enough space to notice experience before choosing.
In a charged hallway, Mara feels the sensation, names it without panic, and decides rather than recoiling or lunging.
A small pause makes thought, dream, urge, and bodily sensation available to judgment instead of command.
The protagonist’s decisive victory is a three-second pause that breaks a socially engineered tempo.
Chastity is presented as a condition for perceiving sensual beauty clearly, not as a flight from beauty.
The prose lingers on hands, breath, fabric, and the beloved’s body precisely when the characters choose restraint.
Integrated desire intensifies affection because delight is no longer split between appetite and personhood.
A scene after refusal grows warmer, funnier, and more playful instead of collapsing into punishment or sulking.
Unmarried attraction can become skilled care, honor, and fascination rather than pseudo-marital entitlement.
Jonah’s courtship is compelling because his attention increases Mara’s freedom and competence.
MPC-08 — Desire must be discerned, even within commitment
Relationship status does not sanctify every impulse; love still asks where desire came from and what it will do to the other.
A married secondary couple provides the mature counterpoint to Fulcrum’s doctrine that consent makes every appetite wise.
MPC-09 — Ask whether the desire is good
Desire is evaluated by love, goodness, timing, and honor; a no can let a provoked impulse fade without denying erotic life.
Mara distinguishes wanting Jonah from wanting to use Jonah to repair humiliation after a public loss.
MPC-10 — Holiness as fascination, not sterility
The prayed-for fruit is a pure, reverent fascination for the other—not indifference.
Prayer does not cool the romantic current; it makes the characters’ attention less grasping and more exact.
MPC-11 — Authority that does not override the will
Divine authority is described as honoring the human capacity to choose rather than coercing, manipulating, or overriding it.
Miriam proves spiritual authority by defending Mara’s no when institutional leaders call refusal evidence of a block.
Satisfied in God, VA Beach, Nov 2025 — Session 4 • mpc-74e7842c6f30540d8f5a-b000019 • [open source](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1063365119)
When identity and blessing are demanded from another person, care itself can become an instrument of control.
A Fulcrum facilitator offers eerily perfect care that quietly makes dissent feel like betrayal.
Satisfied in God, VA Beach, Nov 2025 — Session 4 • mpc-74e7842c6f30540d8f5a-b000043 • [open source](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1063365119)
MPC-13 — Right speech is born from silence
Silence is an active complement to speech and a condition for language that is awake, loving, and true.
Mara wins a verbal contest by refusing the offered frame, waiting, and asking one clean question.
For Talking Beasts: Begin with Silence • mpc-e351064b2f36ff9d0268-b000018 • [open source](https://ministriesofpastoralcare.com/1262-2/)
Silence functions as a gathering-up space where received words can be tested before they become action.
A dorm-room silence lets Mara notice which accusation is hers, which belongs to the group, and which remains unknown.
For Talking Beasts: Begin with Silence • mpc-e351064b2f36ff9d0268-b000020 • [open source](https://ministriesofpastoralcare.com/1262-2/)
MPC-15 — Self-acceptance breaks the internal scoreboard
Receiving identity from divine love displaces narrow, demanding self-measurement and makes growth possible.
Mara stops treating beauty, virginity, cleverness, and male attention as a composite score she must defend.
Mercy received deeply becomes courageous self-acceptance rather than excuse-making.
After a real mistake, Mara admits it before the rival can weaponize it, repairs the harm, and remains upright.
MPC-17 — Repentance includes boundaries and correction
Confession becomes credible through changed conduct, appropriate boundaries, and concrete transformation.
An apology fails until the apologizer surrenders access, accepts witnesses, and changes the procedure.
True restoration creates a transformed relationship; it does not merely return people to the conditions that produced harm.
The resolution preserves mercy while ending the old Fulcrum intimacy regime.
MPC-19 — Forgiveness and reconciliation are distinct
Forgiveness does not require renewed proximity; collapsing it into reconciliation can keep a person trapped in dysfunction.
Mara forgives a betrayer without restoring private access, preserving both tenderness and exit rights.
Forgiveness, the Currency of Relationship — Session 6 • mpc-b3a5e007a6b8809f9ebc-b000020 • [open source](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1092329057)
Mature discernment seeks truth without paranoia and resists deception without becoming hostile.
The climax turns on Mara keeping multiple explanations live long enough to gather witnesses and records.
The Gospel According to Christ • mpc-404d637e0d451d2b2e1b-b000006 • [open source](https://ministriesofpastoralcare.com/the-gospel-according-to-christ/)
B. Leverage and social-influence case-dynamic cards
LEV-01 — Apparent telepathy from involuntary cues
Tiny tactile, postural, vocal, and visual signals can carry more information than participants consciously notice, producing feats that feel paranormal.
Fulcrum students locate a hidden object through a calibration game; Mara experiences the reader as inside her mind.
Use new tasks, composite researchers, and an adult fellowship. Preserve only the cue-channel mechanism and felt eeriness.
Performance can remain impressive until the relevant information channel is isolated; randomization and cue controls distinguish skill from story.
Mara silently changes the rules of a demonstration and watches an oracle become merely talented.
Invent the protocol and result. Keep the epistemic turn: a mundane mechanism need not make the experience emotionally mundane.
Holding an intention to tell the truth while speaking can produce felt ease, strain, resistance, or mismatch that practitioners treat as evidence about underlying belief.
A facilitator asks Mara to repeat a claim until her body gives the approved answer; she later reclaims the exercise alone in prayer.
Change all prompts and actors. Treat the felt signal as data interpreted by characters, never as an infallible oracle.
Blinking, hesitancy, fidgeting, smiles, tempo, and emphasis can be recruited as signs of an internal clash—especially by an observer.
A charismatic reader narrates Mara’s micro-reactions faster than she can contest the interpretation.
The fictional danger comes from interpretive authority and pace, not from copying any real training script.
LEV-05 — Words select different inner objects
Near-synonyms can evoke different concepts and bodily responses; a method can confuse word-choice effects with discovery of hidden truth.
A single loaded word turns a neutral report into an apparent confession, and Mara exposes the switch.
Build a fresh vocabulary for Fulcrum and make semantic ambiguity part of the mystery.
Expectations about what will happen can act as an attentional lens, changing which threats, affordances, and interpretations become salient.
Two teams watch the same interaction under opposite predictions and leave with incompatible but internally coherent stories.
Use a fictional alignment exercise and let the divergence reshape alliances and romantic trust.
LEV-07 — Introspection can become avoidance theater
On charged topics, people may change subjects, forget questions, generate spurious material, or shut down; the group may overinterpret this as proof of a hidden structure.
Mara’s exhaustion during a late-night session is redescribed as resistance, which authorizes a deeper intervention.
Composite the dynamic and keep several explanations alive: fatigue, shame, suggestion, strategy, trauma, or spiritual pressure.
LEV-08 — Shared mental content is hard to adjudicate
Claims of shared content depend on skill judgments, blindspot theories, compatibility checks, confidence reads, and social context—each introducing new inference.
A three-person reading feels convergent until the transcript shows that each answer was subtly repaired after the fact.
Create fictional terminology and preserve the nested-inference structure as the scene’s reveal.
LEV-09 — Sensitization changes the social world
Training can make subtle signals newly vivid while also creating runaway feedback, unpleasant information streams, and escalating suspicion.
After weeks of practice, the cohort cannot stop reading one another; every breath becomes evidence and ordinary friendship becomes exhausting.
Combine the research report with James’s three-practice stabilization model and invent the failure cascade.
On Intention Research; On Training Energy Awareness • [open source](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GCf0XSom_6m09gaYpWqjWtvruwGo_oseGQw0Es2t10s/edit)
LEV-10 — Narrative warfare under charismatic asymmetry

World-saving urgency, teacher–student asymmetry, confession culture, rarity narratives, insularity, and pressure over personal interpretation can make the institution’s story outrank a member’s perception.
Fulcrum does not forbid departure; it makes departure mean cowardice, epistemic failure, and abandonment of humanity.
Recombine dynamics across sources into a new institution, chronology, leadership structure, and crisis. No real person maps one-to-one.
My Experience with Leverage Research; Leverage 1.0 Postmortem Inquiry • [open source](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M4JzeGEaaUyf7Fzl4hi342kwtOHwYGK45WW0RSqjq80/edit)
